html:
Robben Island, in Table Bay off Cape Town, was used for centuries as a place of banishment, and from 1961 to 1991 as a maximum security prison for opponents of apartheid.

Earlier the Dutch and British sent prisoners there, among them Khoekhoe leaders and the Xhosa prophet Makhanda, and it held a leper colony. Under apartheid black political prisoners broke lime in a quarry and lived in harsh conditions. Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in prison there, after the Rivonia Trial.

Prisoners organised study and debate, and it was called the university of the struggle. The last political prisoners left in 1991. It became a museum in 1997 and a UNESCO site in 1999, a symbol of the victory of democracy in South Africa.
sum: Robben Island, in Table Bay off Cape Town, was used for centuries as a place of banishment, and from 1961 to 1991 as a maximum security prison for opponents of apartheid.
